clue.text: Firmly fix length of wood, blue

parts.note: a batten is a long strip of sawn timber
blue means sad or low, i.e. down

explanation.surface: A carpenter's shopping list: a piece of wood and some blue paint, ready to fix something firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like a colour for the wood, but it means low-spirited.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure tightly, as a ship's hatches are made fast before a storm, is the meaning of this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Either way, it's a careless mistake

definitions.note: a silly blunder or gaffe, which reads the same forwards and backwards

indicators.note: read from either end the same letters appear, so the word is a palindrome

parts.note: a silly blunder or gaffe, which reads the same forwards and backwards

explanation.surface: Whichever way you look at it, someone has slipped up through carelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial noun for a silly blunder or gaffe.

clue.text: Plonk! Put down for discussion and heard complaint

parts.note: to table a motion is to put it forward for debate (British usage)

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for complaint is only spoken, so its sound is taken

parts.note: a whine is a moaning complaint

explanation.surface: Someone banging something down at a meeting, raising a matter and grumbling about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plonk!' reads as a thud, but it is British slang for cheap wine. WHINE and WINE sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Plonk is British slang for cheap everyday wine served with meals.

clue.text: Praise former tax cut

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: cut says the word for tax loses its final letter

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy, here for road use

explanation.surface: A politician applauding an old tax reduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks TOLL to TOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud or speak highly of someone is a synonym of praise.

clue.text: Pulled, when cross-dressed?

definitions.meaning: dressed in clothes of the opposite sex, i.e. in drag

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a playful coinage: someone in drag could be said to be 'dragged up'.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of haul along; and being in drag, a performer's cross-dressing outfit.

clue.text: Who might waste a lot of time serving people?

definitions.text: Who might waste a lot of time serving people?

parts.words: Who might waste a lot of time serving people?
parts.note: people who serve in restaurants spend their time standing around in attendance, so they seem to idle while serving

explanation.surface: A grumble about slow service staff dawdling.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that those who serve spend their shifts hanging about until called.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurant staff who serve diners spend much time standing by in attendance.

clue.text: Losing time, walk to find way up?

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the word for walk

parts.note: to tramp is to walk heavily or a long way

explanation.surface: A hiker short of time looking for a quick route up a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloping surface lets you go up from one level to another, an inclined way upward.

clue.text: Emerge with a pay increase

parts.note: a rise is the British word for a salary increase (a raise in the US)

explanation.surface: An employee coming out of the boss's office with a raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To come up or come into being is a synonym of emerge.

clue.text: Fine case in which footballers might be seen?

definitions.text: in which footballers might be seen
definitions.note: a relative phrase describing a place, standing for the noun

parts.note: a fine is a penalty imposed for wrongdoing
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A legal case about a fine, oddly involving footballers.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the definition is a place described by a relative clause; read it as 'place in which footballers might be seen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The marked area in front of each goal on a football pitch is where most attacking play happens.

clue.text: Pressure as Balkan approaches unknown man in the street?

indicators.note: approaches says the Balkan person comes right up to the unknown letter, placing it just before it

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
a Serb is a native of Serbia, a Balkan country
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns x, y, z

explanation.surface: Under pressure, a man from the Balkans approaches a stranger in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man in the street' looks like scene-setting but is the definition: an ordinary member of the public.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinary passing pedestrian, a member of the public walking along, is someone going past.

clue.text: Circle, or segment

parts.note: a bit is a piece or segment of something

explanation.surface: A geometry choice: draw a circle, or just a segment of one.
explanation.definitionFit: To go round something in a curved path, as a planet does the sun, is to circle it.

clue.text: Tito again in turmoil, showing nervousness

indicators.note: in turmoil says the letters of the preceding words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Marshal Tito, Yugoslavia's leader, in trouble yet again and visibly anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitation is a state of anxiety or nervous excitement, a synonym of nervousness.

clue.text: Nightie e.g. in centre of bed, tangled with leg

indicators.note: tangled says the collected letters are jumbled together like bedclothes
centre of picks the middle letter of the word for a sleeping place

explanation.surface: A nightdress caught up around someone's leg in the middle of the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' jumbles EG, IN, E (middle of bed) and LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, flimsy woman's nightdress or dressing gown is a type of nightie.

clue.text: Period that's quiet in trade

indicators.note: in says the letter for quiet goes inside the word for trade

parts.note: to sell is to trade goods
P is the musical marking piano, soft or quiet

explanation.surface: A quiet spell in business, a lull in trading.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of time, such as a dry spell, is a period.

clue.text: Short delay after call, then fix old radio

indicators.note: after places the shortened delay after the call

parts.note: to cry out is to call

indicators.note: short says the word for delay loses its final letter

parts.note: to stall is to delay
to set is to fix firmly in place

explanation.surface: Someone shouts, waits a moment, then repairs an antique wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' docks STALL to STAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An early simple wireless receiver using a crystal detector, popular in the 1920s.

clue.text: Was ruler pelted, as stated?

indicators.note: as stated tells us the word for pelted is spoken, so its sound counts

parts.note: it pelted down means it rained heavily

explanation.surface: A query whether a monarch was pelted with missiles, as reported.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who held the throne ruled during that time.

clue.text: They're authorised to certify stuff: not something to do with astrology

parts.note: Aries, the ram, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Officials who certify documents insisting they have no truck with horoscopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawyers licensed to witness signatures and attest documents are commissioned for that purpose.

clue.text: Swell railway: just the place for a doctor

definitions.text: just the place for a doctor

parts.note: a surge is a swell, as of the sea

explanation.surface: An enthusiast saying a railway is splendid, the perfect spot for a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' poses as the American adjective for 'great' but is a noun. A surgery is the British word for a doctor's consulting room.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a GP sees patients in consulting rooms known by this name.

clue.text: Terrible income, so finally choose to save

indicators.note: terrible says the following letters are in a dreadful mess
finally picks the last letter of the word for choosing

explanation.surface: Someone with a dreadful income deciding to tighten their belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges INCOME SO into ECONOMIS; 'finally' adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut back on spending and be thrifty is to put money by.

clue.text: Affected by bacteria round top of commode? One's not convinced

indicators.note: round says the infected word goes around the letter taken from the commode

parts.note: septic means infected with bacteria

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the toilet chair word

explanation.surface: A toilet seat crawling with germs, and someone unconvinced it is clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubter who questions accepted claims is someone not easily persuaded.

clue.text: Two females: one employed to herd cattle

definitions.meaning: a cow is a female bovine and a girl a young female, read as two words side by side
a woman who works on a ranch tending cattle

explanation.surface: Two women, one of whom works rounding up cattle on a ranch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two females' gives COW plus GIRL, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman ranch hand who tends and drives herds on horseback.

clue.text: Go it alone and the sky's the limit!

definitions.meaning: a playful hint at a lone pilot alone in the air with nothing but sky around

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic nod to a pilot's first unaccompanied flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Act independently without help; literally, pilot an aircraft without an instructor.

clue.text: Unusually gifted, initially schoolboy is restless

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the next word appear in an unusual order
initially picks the first letter of the pupil word

explanation.surface: A gifted schoolboy who cannot sit still in class.
explanation.definitionFit: To squirm and fidget is to be unable to keep still, a sign of restlessness.

clue.text: Embroiled in conflict, some draw tanks retreating

indicators.note: retreating says the letters taken are read backwards, as a retreating army goes back
some says only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: An army drawing its tanks back from the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes RAWTA from 'draw tanks'; 'retreating' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A country engaged in hostilities against another is fighting a war.

clue.text: One barking, not loudly, could be Romeo?

indicators.note: not says the letter for loudly is removed

parts.note: a woofer is a jokey word for a dog, one that barks
F is forte, the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A quiet dog that might be named Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo, Shakespeare's lover, is an example; 'could be' signals that.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Romeo courts Juliet, so he is an example of a suitor.

clue.text: Soundly pack timber for this expensive china

indicators.note: soundly tells us the word for pack is only heard, so its sound counts

parts.note: to wedge is to pack something tightly in
wood is timber

explanation.surface: Instructions to pack fine porcelain carefully with wooden packing.
explanation.walkthrough: Wedgwood is a famous English pottery founded by Josiah Wedgwood.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand of fine English pottery and porcelain, known for blue jasperware.

clue.text: Used to be tense, discontented? Rubbish!

parts.note: was is the past tense of be

indicators.note: discontented means emptied of its contents, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: A grumble about being tense and unhappy, dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' looks like a mood, but it empties 'tense' to TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse, garbage or useless matter is rubbish.

clue.text: Runners touch, with third (or fourth) moving into first place

indicators.text: with third (or fourth) moving into first place
indicators.note: the clue says one of the two identical letters in third or fourth position moves to the front

parts.note: a kiss is a light touch, as in snooker

explanation.surface: Racers touching, with the third-placed runner moving into the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Runners here are not athletes but the long narrow blades used on snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Skis slide over snow, like the runners of a sledge.

clue.text: Sort of headgear to use when one is smoking?

definitions.text: to use when one is smoking
definitions.meaning: a metal pipe carrying smoke away from a stove

explanation.definitionFit: A tall silk hat like Lincoln's, named after the flue pipe of a stove.

clue.text: Problem when Queen leaves, creating fuss

indicators.note: leaves says the Queen's letters depart from the word for problem

parts.note: a stinker is a very difficult problem
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Trouble at court when the monarch walks out and causes an uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick up a commotion or row is to make a big fuss.

clue.text: Sailor heads north for lake

indicators.note: heads says the sailor goes ahead of the letter for north

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor heading north towards a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A tarn is a small mountain lake, common in the English Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mountain lake, especially in northern England.

clue.text: Does their work make them go totally up the wall?

definitions.text: Does their work make them go totally up the wall?

parts.words: Does their work make them go totally up the wall?
parts.note: these workers spread coating over walls, and being plastered is slang for drunk, i.e. totally gone

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a job drives its workers mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go up the wall' means go mad, but these tradesmen literally work up walls; 'plastered' is slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradesmen who apply smooth coatings to walls and ceilings.
